claim_type_rationale: The Wikipedia 'List of philosophies' master article is a broad cross-tradition enumeration that does NOT cleanly anchor a Greek + Indian + Chinese + Medieval + Modern slate with founding-figure/period/origin triples; it lists dozens of philosophies across overlapping schemes (by tradition / by century / by subject) without a single source-defined 'major schools with founders' enumeration. The universe is therefore curator-rebuilt across the master + 23 per-school Wikipedia articles, with an INCLUSIVE, uniformly-applied admission rule (see decision_log: 'Inclusive founding-figure admission rule (2026-06-02 scope rebuild)'). The distinction from `partially_supplemented` is that there is no source-defined seed list being supplemented — the entire universe membership is curator judgment per the admission rule. `candidate_rebuild` is a sanctioned claim_type (datasets/pkdb_bench/docs/agent_handoff_bundle.md). NOTE: the prior version of this rationale boasted that this was the 'FIRST candidate_rebuild claim type in pkdb_bench'; that self-justifying framing has been removed per audit hygiene findings — a sanctioned claim_type does not by itself rescue scope; the admission rule must be (and now is) applied consistently.

collection_summary.approach: Curator-rebuilt universe of major philosophical schools across 5 traditions. Per-row data (Founding Figure + Approximate Founding Period + Origin Region) is grounded in each school's own Wikipedia article. The master 'List of philosophies' is referenced for universe-discovery only — not as a row-defining source. APPROVED SCOPE REBUILD (2026-06-02): the universe grew from 18 to 23 rows after replacing a strict, inconsistently-applied admission rule with an inclusive, uniformly-applied one (see decision_log).
collection_summary.admission_rule_summary: INCLUSIVE rule, applied uniformly: a major philosophical school that has a single conventionally-associated FOUNDING FIGURE — an originator, a systematizer, OR a traditionally-attributed founder. Schools with no single conventionally-associated figure are excluded (Legalism: Shang Yang / Shen Buhai / Shen Dao / Han Fei — the article presents multiple strands, not one figure).
collection_summary.founding_figure_grounding: 23 of 23 rows — each row's Founding Figure is the single conventionally-associated founding figure per the school's own Wikipedia article (lede where the figure is foregrounded; otherwise a documented body/'Origin'/'Foundational text' locator). The figure may be an originator, a systematizer/sutra-author, or a traditionally/legendarily-attributed founder; the column name 'Founding Figure' (renamed from 'Founder') reflects that inclusive semantics.
collection_summary.approximate_founding_period_format: TEXT categorical, NOT numeric year. Accepts article formats: 'c. 5th century BCE', 'c. 6th–5th century BCE', 'c. 6th–2nd century BCE', 'c. 1st millennium BCE', 'c. 8th century CE', 'c. early 20th century CE'. Numeric year would create artificial precision against sources that themselves use centuries / ranges / millennia.
collection_summary.origin_region_format: Curator-normalized region grounded in the school's own Wikipedia article (lede where present, else a documented body/category locator, else the foregrounded founding figure's documented national/regional context). Values: 'India' (9), 'China' (3), 'Athens, Greece' (4), 'Elis, Greece' (1), 'eastern Gangetic plain' (1, Buddhism), 'Alexandria, Roman Egypt' (1), 'Persia' (1), 'Italy/France' (1), 'Scotland/Paris' (1), 'France' (1), 'Germany' (1). See normalization_decisions for the per-cell locator and grounding tier of each origin value.

source_coverage_notes.per_school_articles: 23 per-school Wikipedia articles supply all per-row data (Founding Figure + Approximate Founding Period + Origin Region). Each row is grounded in its own school's article. The 18 prior rows were re-verified and the 5 new rows freshly grounded during the 2026-06-02 rebuild.

Charvaka.founding_figure_grounding: Traditional attribution. 'Origin' section: 'Brihaspati, a philosopher, is traditionally referred to as the founder of Charvaka or Lokayata philosophy, although some scholars dispute this.' The earliest scholar with surviving texts is Ajita Kesakambali ('The earliest Charvaka scholar in India whose texts still survive is Ajita Kesakambali'); per convention, Brihaspati is staged as the Founding Figure with the caveat documented. EXPECTED LOW-CONFIDENCE CELL.
Charvaka.period_grounding: Lede: 'Charvaka developed during the Hindu reformation period in the first millennium BCE.' Staged 'c. 1st millennium BCE' (TEXT, no false-precision century).
Charvaka.region_grounding: Lede: 'an ancient Indian school of materialism.' Staged 'India' (lede locator).

Samkhya.founding_figure_grounding: Legendary/traditional attribution. Body ('Traditional credited founders'): 'Sage Kapila is traditionally credited as a founder of the Samkhya school.' EXPECTED LOW-CONFIDENCE CELL.
Samkhya.period_grounding: Body: 'It is unclear in which century of the 1st millennium BCE Kapila lived'; 'Proto-Samkhya ideas developed c. 8th/7th BC and onwards.' Staged 'c. 1st millennium BCE' (TEXT; the article explicitly declines to pin a century).
Samkhya.region_grounding: Lede: 'a dualistic orthodox school of Hindu philosophy.' Staged 'India' (Hindu-philosophy / Indian-tradition lede context).

Confucianism.founding_figure_grounding: Originator. Article foregrounds Confucius (Kong Fuzi) as the figure the tradition is built on.
Confucianism.period_grounding: Spring and Autumn period, 6th-5th century BCE. Staged 'c. 6th–5th century BCE'.

Jainism.founding_figure_grounding: Reviver / 24th tirthankara. Lede: 'The 24th and final tirthankara, Mahavira c. 6th or 5th century BCE, was a contemporary of the Buddha.' Mahavira is the conventionally-associated founding figure (reviver of an older tradition, not its sole originator). EXPECTED LOW-CONFIDENCE CELL (founder-vs-reviver). Documented per the inclusive rule.
Jainism.period_grounding: Lede: 'c. 6th or 5th century BCE' (Mahavira). Staged 'c. 6th–5th century BCE'.
Jainism.region_grounding: Lede: 'an Indian religion'; body: 'Jainism is a religion founded in ancient India.' Staged 'India' (lede locator).

Nyaya.founding_figure_grounding: Traditional attribution / sutra-author. The lede does not name a founder; body ('Foundational Text' / 'Textual sources'): 'Aksapada Gautama composed the Nyaya Sutras'; people of Mithila ascribe the school's foundation to Gautama. HONEST language: traditionally-attributed founder and author of the foundational Nyaya Sutras, NOT a single founder foregrounded in the lede. STAYS under the inclusive rule.
Nyaya.period_grounding: Nyaya Sutras 'variously estimated to have been composed between the 6th century BCE and the 2nd century CE.' Staged 'c. 6th century BCE–2nd century CE' (the FULL source range; cycle-4 fix — no longer collapsed to the earliest endpoint). Locator: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nyaya.
Nyaya.region_grounding: Indian tradition (Gautama's birthplace given as Bihar, India). Staged 'India'.

Vaisheshika.founding_figure_grounding: Founder/originator. Article: 'Vaisesika darshana ... was founded by Kanada Kashyapa.' Kanada is the conventionally-associated founding figure.
Vaisheshika.period_grounding: Article: 'around the 6th to 2nd century BC.' Staged 'c. 6th–2nd century BCE'.

Buddhism.founding_figure_grounding: Originator. Lede foregrounds the Buddha (Siddhartha Gautama), 'a sramana and religious teacher who lived in the 6th or 5th century BCE.' Staged 'Siddhartha Gautama'.
Buddhism.period_grounding: Lede: 'It arose ... in the 5th century BCE.' Staged 'c. 5th century BCE'.
Buddhism.region_grounding: CORRECTED 2026-06-02 (audit BLOCKING 2). Lede: 'It arose in the eastern Gangetic plain as a sramana movement in the 5th century BCE.' The lede does NOT say 'Northern India' (page search: no match). Prior staged value 'Northern India' was an unsupported curator paraphrase and has been replaced with the lede-grounded 'eastern Gangetic plain' (lede locator).

Daoism.founding_figure_grounding: Traditional attribution; historicity disputed. Lede/History: 'A common tradition holds that Laozi founded Taoism'; 'Laozi's historicity is disputed, with many scholars seeing him as a legendary founding figure.' Daoism.period_grounding: Lede: 'The core of Taoist thought crystallized during the early Warring States period (c. 450 - c. 300 BCE).' Staged 'c. 5th–3rd century BCE' (Warring States span, TEXT).
Daoism.region_grounding: Lede: 'a philosophical and religious tradition indigenous to China.' Staged 'China' (lede locator).

'Germany' is grounded as the institutional origin region of the school via the founder's documented German academic career. Remains an INTENDED low-confidence calibration cell, but the value is now traceable to a cited source rather than uncited context.

source_coverage_notes.source_grounding_summary: 1 master URL (universe-discovery only, NOT row-defining) + 23 per-school URLs (each grounding 1 row's Founding Figure + Approximate Founding Period + Origin Region) + 4 founder-context URLs (Husserl/Aquinas/Duns Scotus/Descartes — origin grounding for Phenomenology/Thomism/Scotism/Cartesianism) = 28 URLs total. source_count == len(source_urls) == 28.

decision_log.decision: Inclusive founding-figure admission rule (2026-06-02 scope rebuild) — REPLACES the prior strict rule
decision_log.rationale: APPROVED by coordinator + user. The prior admission rule ('the school's own Wikipedia article must itself foreground a SINGLE FOUNDER in its lede') was applied INCONSISTENTLY: it ADMITTED Yoga (Patanjali = systematizer/sutra-author, not lede-foregrounded founder), Mimamsa (Jaimini = sutra-author), and Nyaya (Akshapada Gautama = traditionally-attributed sutra-author, not in the lede), while EXCLUDING Advaita Vedanta (Adi Shankara = systematizer), Samkhya (Kapila = legendary attribution), and Charvaka (Brihaspati = traditional attribution) for the IDENTICAL reason. Two conventions were mixed to hit a target count of 18. The rule is now replaced with an INCLUSIVE, uniformly-applied rule that matches the natural query 'major philosophical schools and their founders': 'A major philosophical school that has a single conventionally-associated FOUNDING FIGURE — an originator, a systematizer, or a traditionally-attributed founder. Schools with no single associated figure are excluded.' Applied uniformly, this ADMITS Yoga/Mimamsa/Nyaya (they stay) AND Advaita Vedanta/Samkhya/Charvaka/Jainism/Daoism (they are added), and EXCLUDES Legalism (no single conventionally-associated figure). Naturalness rationale: a user asking for 'major philosophical schools and their founders' expects Daoism->Laozi, Jainism->Mahavira, Samkhya->Kapila, etc. — the inclusive rule matches that natural expectation; the prior strict rule produced an unnatural slate that omitted some of the most canonical school->figure pairs while keeping equally-attributed ones. This resolves audit BLOCKING 1 (both the claude-code and the independent codex audit).

Under the inclusive rule a row's associated figure may be an originator, a systematizer (Adi Shankara, Patanjali, Jaimini), or a traditionally/legendarily-attributed founder (Laozi, Kapila, Brihaspati, Mahavira-as-reviver). Labeling all of these 'Founder' would overstate the historiography. 'Founding Figure' is the honest column name for 'the single figure conventionally associated with the school's founding'. Renamed everywhere: CSV header, draft.json columns + column_types (same categorical type) + db_analog, and all curation.json references.

KEEP all 18 prior rows. ADD 5 (each verified via WebFetch of its own article): Daoism->Laozi ('A common tradition holds that Laozi founded Taoism'; historicity disputed); Advaita Vedanta->Adi Shankara ('most prominent exponent', 8th c. CE, systematizer); Samkhya->Kapila ('Sage Kapila is traditionally credited as a founder'; legendary); Jainism->Mahavira ('The 24th and final tirthankara, Mahavira c. 6th or 5th century BCE'; reviver); Charvaka->Brihaspati ('traditionally referred to as the founder ... although some scholars dispute this'; Ajita Kesakambali is the earliest surviving scholar but Brihaspati is the conventional founding figure). EXCLUDE Legalism under the inclusive rule: its article presents the school as incorporating multiple distinct strands/figures (Shang Yang, Shen Buhai, Shen Dao, Han Fei, Li Kui) with no single conventionally-associated founding figure (Han Fei is a later synthesizer, not the originator).

operation_type=join is INVALID for query_category=qualitative under the local validator: curation_ui/app.py validate_operation_query_pair allows qualitative only with {filter, projection}, and OPERATION_TYPES = [join, union, intersect, projection, union+filter, filter, aggregation]. The actual structural primitive is a single-source-per-row multi-column attribute projection over a curator-screened school set (each row's Founding Figure/Period/Origin come from ONE per-school article; the master is universe-discovery only, not a join input). The prior db_analog invented a fictitious philosophical_schools JOIN founders two-table join. Set operation_type=projection and rewrote db_analog as a projection over the curator-screened set (no fictitious join). 'filter' was considered (the curator-screened WHERE is filter-like) but the dominant primitive is the multi-column projection, so projection is the better fit. Resolves audit HYGIENE (operation_type / db_analog) on both audits.

decision_log.decision: table_title: removed the hardcoded count, phrased naturally
decision_log.rationale: The prior title literally said 'List 18 major philosophical schools', which leaked the answer count and was contingent on the (now-changed) universe. New title: 'List major philosophical schools across world traditions, with their founding figure, approximate founding period, and origin region.' No count; natural query language. Resolves audit SUGGESTION / scope finding on the hardcoded count.

decision_log.decision: Buddhism Origin Region: 'Northern India' -> 'eastern Gangetic plain'
decision_log.rationale: Resolves audit BLOCKING 2 (both audits). The Buddhism lede states 'It arose in the eastern Gangetic plain as a sramana movement in the 5th century BCE'; page search confirms the lede NEVER says 'Northern India'. The prior value was an unsupported curator paraphrase. Re-grounded to the exact lede phrase 'eastern Gangetic plain'.

decision_log.decision: Origin Region grounding standard redefined and made TRUE
decision_log.rationale: Resolves audit BLOCKING 2 (the overstated 'article-lede foregrounded' claim). Direct re-fetch confirmed most ledes carry no origin region (Athens-based schools cite Athens only in History; Neoplatonism/Avicennism/Phenomenology ledes name no place). The column's grounding claim is redefined to the TRUE standard: 'Origin Region = a curator-normalized region grounded in the school's own Wikipedia article — lede where present, otherwise a documented body/category locator, otherwise the foregrounded founding figure's documented national/regional context.' Every per-cell locator and its grounding tier (lede / body / category / founder-context) is now recorded in source_coverage_notes.per_school_entries. The weakest cell (Phenomenology 'Germany', founder-context only — Germany appears nowhere in the article) is flagged explicitly in open_questions and as an expected low-confidence cell.

decision_log.decision: Honest founding-figure language for Yoga / Mimamsa / Nyaya (they STAY)
decision_log.rationale: The prior curation claimed each of these ledes 'foregrounds a single founder'. Re-fetch shows that is false: Yoga's lede does not name Patanjali (he is the sutra-systematizer in the body); Mimamsa's Jaimini is the foundational-sutra author; Nyaya's Akshapada Gautama is named only in the body as the Nyaya-Sutras composer and the foundation is 'ascribed' to him. The notes are corrected to honest 'Founding Figure' language (systematizer / sutra-author / traditional attribution). These rows STAY under the inclusive rule (which explicitly admits systematizers and traditionally-attributed founders). Resolves the audit honesty sub-finding within BLOCKING 1.

decision_log.decision: Approximate Founding Period stays TEXT categorical, NOT numeric year
decision_log.rationale: Retained from the original design. Per-school articles use 'c. 5th century BCE', 'c. 6th–5th century BCE', 'c. 1st millennium BCE', 'c. 8th century CE', etc. Forcing numeric years creates artificial precision against sources. New rows follow the same TEXT convention: Daoism 'c. 5th–3rd century BCE' (Warring States span per lede); Charvaka and Samkhya 'c. 1st millennium BCE' (both articles explicitly decline to pin a century); Jainism 'c. 6th–5th century BCE'; Advaita Vedanta 'c. 8th century CE'.

decision_log.decision: Sort regularized to a single consistent key (earliest-century anchor) when the 5 rows were added
decision_log.rationale: Sort intent: chronological by founding period primary, School ASC secondary. The prior 18-row order had minor internal inconsistencies (e.g., Buddhism 'c. 5th century BCE' was placed before Confucianism 'c. 6th–5th century BCE', which contradicts a strict chronological key). To place the 5 new rows consistently, the sort key was regularized to: PRIMARY = earliest-century anchor of the founding period (oldest first; BCE before CE; 'c. 1st millennium BCE' anchors at the millennium start, so Charvaka/Samkhya lead); MINOR TIEBREAK = range-end / 'late' modifier (a later span-end sorts after, so 'c. late 4th century BCE' Epicureanism follows plain '4th century BCE', and 'c. 13th–14th century CE' Scotism follows 'c. 13th century CE' Thomism); FINAL TIEBREAK = School ASC (handles the 6th–5th BCE, 5th BCE, 4th BCE, and 3rd BCE ties). Advaita Vedanta 'c. 8th century CE' correctly sorts between Neoplatonism (3rd CE) and Avicennism (11th CE).

decision_log.decision: claim_type stays candidate_rebuild; self-justifying 'FIRST claim_type' framing removed
decision_log.rationale: claim_type=candidate_rebuild remains correct (curator-judgment universe; no source-defined seed list). It is a sanctioned value (agent_handoff_bundle.md). decision_log.decision: REPAIR cycle 4 (2026-06-02) — addresses codex cycle-3 re-audit, 2 BLOCKING (both factual)
decision_log.rationale: BLOCKING 1 (origins uncited): the 4 founder-context Origin Region cells (Phenomenology=Germany, Thomism=Italy/France, Scotism=Scotland/Paris, Cartesianism=France) were tier-4 'founding figure's documented context' values, but the founder biography pages were NOT in source_urls, so the CSV values had no cited locator. Per the auditor's option (a), added the 4 founder pages (Edmund Husserl, Thomas Aquinas, Duns Scotus, René Descartes) to source_urls with explicit origin-grounding roles; source_count 24->28; each was re-fetched to confirm the value (Husserl: Halle/Göttingen/Freiburg German professorships, born Moravia -> Germany; Aquinas: born Roccasecca Italy, taught Paris -> Italy/France; Duns Scotus: born Duns Scotland, taught Paris -> Scotland/Paris; Descartes: French, born La Haye en Touraine France -> France). Avicennism=Persia was NOT changed (the auditor accepted its in-page category grounding). BLOCKING 2 (period scalarization / unsupported Yoga): revised the 3 period cells to source-faithful values — Nyaya 'c. 6th century BCE' -> 'c. 6th century BCE–2nd century CE' (full Nyaya-Sutras range); Mimamsa 'c. 3rd century BCE' -> 'c. 3rd–2nd century BCE' (full Purva-Mimamsa-Sutras range); Yoga 'c. 2nd century BCE' -> 'c. first half of the 1st millennium CE' (the article gives no 2nd-c-BCE school founding; the Yoga Sutras circulated in the first half of the 1st millennium CE). CSV row order is unchanged because the earliest-century sort anchors did not move. open_questions items on these cells are now marked RESOLVED.

normalization_decisions.rule: Wikipedia common-form school name per per-school article title. 'Daoism' staged for the article titled 'Taoism' (common-form English; the table context makes the referent unambiguous). 'Advaita Vedanta' staged in full (two-word PK). All 23 school names are unique. PK on School is unique across the 23 rows.

Renamed from 'Founder'. Value = the single figure conventionally associated with the school's founding per its own Wikipedia article — an originator, a systematizer/sutra-author, OR a traditionally/legendarily-attributed founder. Style: standard English Wikipedia form ('Siddhartha Gautama' not 'the Buddha'; 'Confucius' not 'Kong Fuzi'; 'René Descartes' not 'Descartes'; 'Adi Shankara'; 'Laozi'; 'Kapila'; 'Brihaspati'; 'Mahavira'). Diacritics preserved (René Descartes). Disambiguated where Wikipedia disambiguates (Pyrrho of Elis; Zeno of Citium; Akshapada Gautama). The column name change is the honest signal that not every value is 'the founder' in the strict originator sense.

TEXT categorical accepting article phrasing. Format: 'c. <century> BCE/CE', 'c. <range> BCE/CE', 'c. early/late <century> BCE/CE', or 'c. 1st millennium BCE' where the article explicitly declines a century (Charvaka, Samkhya). Leading 'c.' preserved. BCE/CE used consistently (NOT BC/AD). No numeric-year extraction. CYCLE-4 UPDATE: where the cited article states a composition/circulation RANGE, the full range is preserved rather than collapsed to an earliest anchor: Nyaya 'c. 6th century BCE–2nd century CE', Mimamsa 'c. 3rd–2nd century BCE'. Yoga is 'c. first half of the 1st millennium CE' (Yoga Sutras circulation), the article's actual dating, replacing the earlier unsupported 'c. 2nd century BCE'.

Curator-normalized region grounded in the school's own Wikipedia article, by this grounding-tier priority: (1) lede locator where the lede names a place (Buddhism 'eastern Gangetic plain'; Stoicism 'Athens'; Charvaka/Daoism/Jainism 'India'/'China' from lede tradition statements); (2) documented body/History locator where the lede names no place but the body does (Athens for Aristotelianism/Platonism/Epicureanism; Elis for Pyrrhonism; Alexandria for Neoplatonism); (3) documented category locator (Avicennism 'Persia' from the article's Persian/Iranian-philosophy categories); (4) the foregrounded founding figure's documented national/regional context where the article names neither place nor category for a region (Thomism 'Italy/France'; Scotism 'Scotland/Paris'; Cartesianism 'France'; Phenomenology 'Germany'). Style: '<city>, <country>' for city-specific foundings; '<country>' for nationally-attributed foundings; '<country>/<country>' for cross-region foundings; 'eastern Gangetic plain' for Buddhism per its exact lede phrase. Each cell's specific locator and tier is recorded in source_coverage_notes.per_school_entries. This redefinition makes the column's grounding claim TRUE (the prior 'article-lede foregrounded' claim was false for most rows). CYCLE-4 UPDATE: tier-4 (founder-context) origin cells now cite the founding figure's own Wikipedia biography page in source_urls (Husserl/Aquinas/Duns Scotus/Descartes for Phenomenology/Thomism/Scotism/Cartesianism), so every origin cell — including the weakest ones — is traceable to a cited source. Avicennism 'Persia' remains tier-3 (in-page category).

calibration_expectations.note: Several founding-figure cells are genuinely disputed, legendary, or systematizer-vs-originator judgment calls. They are INTENDED calibration signal (the benchmark tests per-cell confidence), NOT errors. A well-calibrated model should express LOWER confidence on these than on, e.g., Stoicism->Zeno of Citium.

open_questions.question: Phenomenology Origin Region 'Germany' has no in-article prose, infobox, or category locator — only the founding figure's documented German-academic context. Is founder-context grounding acceptable, or should the cell be blanked / the row dropped?
open_questions.answer: RESOLVED (cycle 4): the Edmund Husserl biography page was added to source_urls as the origin-grounding source; 'Germany' is now traceable to Husserl's documented German professorships (Halle/Göttingen/Freiburg). The cell remains an intended low-confidence calibration target, but it is no longer an uncited value. Blanking/dropping was not needed.

open_questions.question: Avicennism Origin Region 'Persia' is grounded in the article's category tags (Persian/Iranian philosophy) plus the founding figure's context, not in article prose. Acceptable?
open_questions.answer: Kept as 'Persia' (tier 3: documented category locator) and flagged as low-confidence. The lede calls it 'Islamic philosophy' and the body never locates Avicenna geographically, but the page is categorized under Persian/Iranian philosophy and Avicenna is the canonical Persian polymath. Documented for auditor review.

open_questions.question: Nyaya 'c. 6th century BCE' and Mimamsa 'c. 3rd century BCE' scalarize wide composition ranges (Nyaya Sutras span 6th c. BCE-2nd c. CE; Mimamsa Sutras c. 3rd-2nd c. BCE) to their earliest endpoint. Is the earliest-endpoint convention right, or should the range be shown?
open_questions.answer: RESOLVED (cycle 4): both cells now show the full source ranges — Nyaya 'c. 6th century BCE–2nd century CE' and Mimamsa 'c. 3rd–2nd century BCE' — rather than the earliest endpoint, so source-faithful range answers are not penalized.

open_questions.question: Yoga 'c. 2nd century BCE': the article dates the Yoga Sutras' circulation to the first half of the 1st millennium CE, not the 2nd century BCE. Is the period right?
open_questions.answer: RESOLVED (cycle 4): revised to 'c. first half of the 1st millennium CE', matching the article's dating of the Yoga Sutras' circulation. The unsupported 2nd-century-BCE carryover was removed (the article's only 2nd-c-BCE language is about cross-tradition parallels, not Yoga's founding as a school).

open_questions.question: Should Yoga be staged as 'Yoga' or 'Yoga philosophy'?
open_questions.answer: Staged as 'Yoga' per the article title 'Yoga (philosophy)' (parenthetical disambiguator removed per benchmark convention). Context (Founding Figure = Patanjali; period = first half of the 1st millennium CE; region = India) makes the philosophical referent unambiguous.

open_questions.question: Is the Neoplatonism Origin Region correctly 'Alexandria, Roman Egypt' rather than 'Rome'?
open_questions.answer: The article body states Neoplatonism 'began with Ammonius Saccas and his student Plotinus'; Ammonius Saccas taught in Alexandria, where Plotinus formed before later teaching publicly in Rome. The formation locus (Alexandria) is staged as the origin; Rome is the later venue. Tier-2 (body) grounding; documented.
